chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The guardian of a child fasts on his behalf if he cannot find a sacrificial animal, and he is in the state of Tamattu'.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever upon whom Hajj is obligatory, it is not permissible for him to perform Hajj on behalf of another, and there is no objection if the young one performs Hajj on behalf of the young one if the young one does not have wealth with which to perform Hajj on his own behalf.

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: A state of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for performing Hajj on behalf of a child or another person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* compensation, where a guardian performs fasting on behalf of a child who cannot offer a sacrifice, highlighting the transferability of ritual duties. Shaykh al-Tusi further distinguishes this by noting that while obligatory Hajj is generally personal, a young person (*al-sarrura*) may perform it for another if neither possesses independent wealth, reflecting the Shia juristic view on financial capacity and ritual substitution. This underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding *kaffarah* and *hajj* when economic constraints prevent direct performance.
